items.title: Tesla extends Cybertruck production to late summer 2027 amid fan backlash
items.teaser: Elon Musk now says Tesla will keep building the Cybertruck “through the end of summer 2027” to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” That buys the electric pickup roughly two to three more months, five days after Tesla first announced it was killing it. The reprieve lands as a growing number of Tesla’s own fans push back on the decision, and on what it says about Tesla’s future as a company that sells cars to people.

items.title: SpaceX’s $24B Starbase supercomputer plan slipped past a key roadblock
items.teaser: SpaceX wants a Starbase tax break for a $24 billion gas plant and supercomputer campus.

items.title: Why the data center you dread might never even be built
items.teaser: The data center boom is running into serious real-world obstacles, from widespread local opposition and permitting delays to a scramble for electricity. Before those challenges even come into play, though, there’s a more basic problem: A lot of the projects being announced may never get built in the first place.
